title: Yokohama and Tokyo: a Japanese band and Meiji Park
summary: Billeted at the Mitsubishi yards he hears a Japanese band swing 'The Sergeant Was Shy', then the band stays at Meiji Park in Tokyo.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Oh, man, that was something. We arrived in Okinawa -- I mean, --

MR. PILLARS: -- in Yokahama, and we were billeted in the office of the Mitsubishi yards. The shipbuilding yards. We were billeted right there. And one night, we were walking down the street, and we heard a band playing, and we walked into this barroom, and there was a band playing, swinging like mad, the Japanese, playing 'The Sergeant Was Shy.' And the Japanese
girls were dancing like mad, they all had these silk dresses on. And they treat us real nice. And I said, 'My, my, this is a modern country over here. These people over here are living it up.'

But we were billeted there, we played all around Yokahama, played the various bases. Then we left and went to Tokyo. And we stayed in Meiji Park. That was an Olympic grounds they had built for the Olympic shows they never had on account of the war. It was beautiful out there. And we would go out and play different bases, come back, and they'd serve us a little midnight snack and they would show us movies, before going to bed.
